transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-13
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 41 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Oliver Grant (CISO - Astral), Priya Rao (Head of Infrastructure - Astral), Evan Morales (Cloud Architect - Astral)

Summary (auto):
Quick security posture discovery focused on compliance and deployment options. Customer leans toward dedicated or private due to regulatory requirements but wants to understand hosted tradeoffs and proofs.

Topics (auto):
- Compliance (SOC2/ISO)
- SSO/SAML/SCIM and IdP integration
- RBAC and audit trails
- Encryption and key management
- Data residency & retention policies

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, i'm the account lead, with me is Liam our solutions engineer. you all good for a quick intros?
[00:12] Oliver: yeah hi i'm Oliver, ciso at Astral Finance, i've got Priya our head of infra and Evan who's our cloud architect.
[00:18] Priya: hey everyone, thanks for setting this up.
[00:22] Maya: great, high level we want to understand your security requirements, whether hosted is viable or if you need dedicated or private, and then follow up with artifacts. sound right?
[00:30] Evan: yes, main drivers are compliance and data residency. we handle payment data and we need tight auditability.
[00:35] Liam: quick q — do you currently have SOC 2 type II and any ISO 27001 scope?
[00:40] Oliver: we have soc2 in process, controls mostly in place, expecting attestation q2, iso 27001 is being evaluated but not certified.
[00:50] Maya: cool; from Redwood side we have SOC 2 Type II and an ISO summary, we'll share those docs, that tends to cover hosted for many customers, but we can also discuss dedicated/private for added isolation.
[01:05] Priya: one thing — SSO, SAML support is critical; we need SCIM for provisioning and fine-grained groups. does redwood support that across hosted and private?
[01:14] Liam: yes SSO via SAML or OIDC is supported, SCIM provisioning is available for Dedicated and Private today, for Hosted we have SAML + SSO, SCIM on roadmap for hosted but doable via custom provisioning in the meantime. caveat: for SCIM and SCIM sync with internal idp usually easier on dedicated/private because of network access.
[01:40] Evan: ok, and RBAC? we need least-priv and API key scoping, token rotation.
[01:46] Maya: RBAC supports roles + per-route permissions, you can scope keys to specific models or routes, and we support short-lived tokens and key rotation via our console and APIs.
[01:58] Oliver: audit logs — we need immutable audit trails for all API calls and admin actions, retention for 7 years ideally or ability to export logs to our SIEM.
[02:08] Liam: we write structured audit logs, admin actions, token ops, model changes; Hosted includes log export to S3/logging endpoints and integration with Datadog/Splunk. for Dedicated/Private we can ship logs directly to your SIEM over secure channel. retention default is 90 days but can be extended with add-on or via export.
[02:30] Priya: 90 days default is too short for our needs; can we set longer retention? and is there WORM or tamper-evident options?
[02:38] Liam: yes extendable via enterprise package, and for private you can manage retention internally, for hosted we provide signed logs and options to export to your S3 with lifecycle policies, WORM depends on your S3 settings.
[02:52] Oliver: encryption at rest and in transit — we prefer customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for at-rest encryption.
[02:59] Maya: supported — Hosted supports CMEK via cloud KMS (AWS KMS) for certain enterprise tiers; Dedicated and Private give you more direct KMS integration and HSM options.
[03:10] Evan: if we go dedicated what does network look like? vpc peering? private link?
[03:16] Liam: Dedicated can be set up in your VPC via private link or VPC peering depending on cloud. Private is an on-prem or VPC managed deployment with full control over networking. we'll share a sample network diagram.
[03:30] Priya: data residency — we need to ensure model telemetry and logs never leave eu-west-1. can hosted guarantee region locking?
[03:38] Maya: we have region controls for hosted where data stays in region for in-flight and storage for select customers; Dedicated and Private give full regional control. we'll include region-specific deployments in the doc pack.
[03:52] Oliver: what about model caching and KV cache? could that leak pii into logs?
[03:58] Liam: good question — persistent KV cache is configurable and by default not persisted across model versions; sensitive data should be masked and we have controls to disable caching for specific routes. logs do not store raw model contexts, only metadata and hashes unless configured to persist. i'll follow up with specifics.
[04:20] Evan: how are backups handled, and surrounding retention for tokens and credentials?
[04:25] Liam: backups are encrypted with CMEK, credential rotation is supported via APIs, and secrets are stored in vault-backed stores; for private you can use your vault.
[04:36] Maya: any regulatory specific requirements? pci scope?
[04:39] Oliver: we are in scope for pci-lite for payments and also have internal audit that wants 7 year retention for certain logs, and yearly pen tests.
[04:49] Priya: pen tests — do you support customer-run pen testing on dedicated/private?
[04:53] Liam: yes we have a process: coordinate schedule, scope, run in sandbox/dedicated env, require notification and a short MOU. for hosted there are restrictions.
[05:06] Maya: great — quick note on pricing impact: dedicated and private increase cost but give you isolation and compliance benefits. often customers start hosted with strict controls then move to dedicated.
[05:18] Oliver: timeline — we'd like to pilot in Q2 and decide by end of Q2, is that workable?
[05:25] Maya: yes timeline aligns with our pilot programs.
[05:28] Evan: curious about telemetry for model quality and regressions — we need to know what data is collected.
[05:33] Liam: we collect telemetry for inference metrics (latency, errors) and optional request/response logging for evals; customers can opt-out of request logging and can configure sampling. for Dedicated/Private telemetry can be routed to your observability stack.
[05:50] Priya: network requirements — what's required for VPC peering and firewall rules?
[05:55] Liam: we'll share a network allowlist doc with ports, IPs, and endpoints. Dedicated requires a set of IP ranges and a private link endpoint; private you'll control all egress.
[06:07] Oliver: about data deletion — if we stop service can you guarantee deletion within X days and provide a certificate?
[06:14] Maya: yes we have data deletion procedures, we can provide a deletion certificate and wipe keys; retention and precise SLA depends on contract.
[06:24] Evan: are we able to do a red-team or internal audit on a dedicated instance?
[06:29] Liam: yes, with coordination. for private obviously that's customer-controlled.
[06:33] Priya: curious about SSO groups syncing — can we map AD groups to RBAC roles?
[06:38] Liam: yes group mapping is supported via SCIM and SAML attributes on dedicated/private; hosted supports attribute mapping.
[06:47] Oliver: for auditability we need a clear mapping of admin actions to user ids with immutable timestamps. is that in your audit logs?
[06:55] Liam: yes admin actions include actor id, timestamp, action type, resource affected — logs are immutable once written and include integrity metadata.
[07:05] Maya: ok let's talk about next steps, we'll send SOC2 artifacts and a network diagram, liam will prep a dedicated perf plan and we'll schedule the deeper technical review.
[07:16] Priya: can you also send a sample contract clause for data residency and breach notification?
[07:20] Maya: yes we'll include a sample clause and our standard breach notification timeline.
[07:25] Oliver: thanks, also can you send a list of past customers in finance who did dedicated?
[07:30] Maya: yes with permissions, we'll share references.
[07:33] Evan: small thing — does hosted preserve prompt-level pii in logs by default?
[07:39] Liam: by default request logging is disabled for hosted unless you opt-in; when enabled we recommend field-level redaction and sampling.
[07:50] Priya: ok good.
[07:52] (cross talk)
[08:00] Maya: anything else on compliance?
[08:03] Oliver: just pen test cadence and 3rd party attestations, you covered it.
[08:08] Liam: one more: for KMS we support customer master keys in AWS and GCP, and for private deployments you can bring an HSM. i'll include the exact supported key rotation and CMK ARN patterns in the doc.
[08:25] Priya: perfect.
[08:28] Maya: i'll recap in email and include docs, SOC2, iso summary, network guide, and liam's perf plan.
[08:36] Oliver: thanks everyone.
[08:38] Maya: thanks, we'll follow up with dates for the technical deep dive.
[08:42] (meeting ends)

Note: transcription contains occasional mis-heard words and run-ons; speaker turns may overlap.
